clue.text: Something projecting on cards when without guillotine, ultimately

definitions.text: Something projecting on cards when without guillotine, ultimately

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece set on another follows it

parts.note: a deck is a pack of playing cards

indicators.note: here means outside, so the projecting piece wraps round the next letter

parts.note: a ledge is a shelf or ridge that juts out

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word guillotine

explanation.surface: A remark about the edges of playing cards sticking out when nobody has trimmed them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. The whole clue describes the rough untrimmed border of handmade paper or card, which sticks out because no guillotine has cut it.
explanation.definitionFit: A deckle edge is the ragged untrimmed border of handmade paper or card, left because it was never cut straight.

clue.text: Democrat clique which might be taken out for a meal

definitions.text: which might be taken out for a meal

parts.note: an inner set is an exclusive circle or clique

explanation.surface: A party faction who might be treated to dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken out for a meal' suggests a person being treated, but it is crockery taken out of a cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete set of plates and dishes is brought out of the cupboard for serving a meal.

clue.text: Early jetliner having to arrive before time

parts.note: to come is to arrive

explanation.surface: An early passenger jet that had to land before the scheduled hour.
explanation.definitionFit: The de Havilland Comet was the world's first commercial jet airliner, from the 1950s.

clue.text: Bright light Italian painter's not got right, inappropriate over Venice

parts.note: a laser gives an intense beam of light

indicators.note: not got means the following letter is missing

parts.note: Guido Reni was an Italian Baroque painter; the 's is a link

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the word is read upwards

parts.note: amiss means wrong or inappropriate

explanation.surface: An Italian painter of brilliant light is out of place above the city of Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not got right' takes R from RENI, leaving ENI; 'over' turns AMISS to SSIMA.
explanation.definitionFit: La Serenissima, the most serene, is the historic title of the Venetian republic and so of Venice.

clue.text: Together by bedroom? Sex inside to follow

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to ensue is to follow on
it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: Something racy about a couple next to the bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' as a coy word for sex is an old crossword favourite. The definition is a question because the phrase usually describes a bathroom joined to a bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathroom described this way is attached to the bedroom, joined with it together in one suite.

clue.text: Greatly appreciated garland sent up to good actor

indicators.note: in a down clue sent up means the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: dug is slang for appreciated or liked a lot
a lei is a Hawaiian garland

explanation.surface: A garland is thrown up to a fine actor who was greatly applauded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' turns DUG, LEI and G as one run. John Gielgud was a great English stage actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Gielgud was one of the leading English actors of the twentieth century.

clue.text: What tropical monsoon will break?

indicators.note: the two words break open to show a run of letters straddling them

explanation.surface: A question about what a tropical rainy season will shatter.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across the join in 'tropiCAL Monsoon'. A monsoon breaking also ends a spell of still weather, so the whole clue is the definition too.
explanation.definitionFit: Still, settled weather is what the arrival of the monsoon rains brings to an end.

clue.text: Show regret where a game soldier is given Ecstasy

parts.note: polo is a game played on horseback
a GI is an American soldier, and GI's stands for GI is
E is the abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Saying sorry when a soldier at a sports match is handed drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soldier is' gives GI'S, the GI plus the contracted is.
explanation.definitionFit: To apologise is to express regret for something done.

clue.text: Teachers' leader in pretence to be up in subject

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading upwards
one piece is put in the other

parts.note: a sham is a pretence

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: The head of teachers pretending to be good at a school subject.
explanation.walkthrough: T from 'Teachers' goes 'in' SHAM to give SHTAM, which 'to be up' turns over.
explanation.definitionFit: Mathematics is a school subject, shortened to this in British English.

clue.text: Downfall making sin seem terrible

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad way, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A moralising line that sinning brings about one's ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges SIN and SEEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A nemesis is the agent of someone's ruin, and by extension the ruin or undoing itself.

clue.text: Make use of plan, largely in escape route

indicators.note: one piece is put in the other

parts.note: an exit is a way out

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a plot is a plan or scheme

explanation.surface: Advice to take advantage of a plan that is mostly about getting out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' trims PLOT to PLO, which goes 'in' EXIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit something is to take advantage of it or put it to use.

clue.text: Near result of cash squeeze?

definitions.meaning: near is old slang for stingy or mean with money
the act of squeezing coins, read literally as pinching pennies

explanation.walkthrough: 'Near' looks like the opposite of far, but it means miserly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being penny-pinching means being stingy, and near is an old word for exactly that.

clue.text: Key Conservative from heart of America

indicators.note: the Conservative abbreviation is taken away from the next piece

parts.note: the centre spelt the American way is center

explanation.surface: A claim about a crucial Tory hailing from the American heartland.
explanation.walkthrough: The American spelling CENTER loses its C. 'Key' looks like an adjective (crucial), but it is a key on a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The Enter key is one of the keys on a computer keyboard.

clue.text: Displaying art centrally in King's Benin house

indicators.note: centrally means the middle letters of each of the next three words, dropping their ends

explanation.surface: A description of artwork shown in the palace of the King of Benin.
explanation.walkthrough: The middles of kINGs, bENIn and hOUSe give ING, ENI and OUS. The famous Benin Bronzes make the royal art scene plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Art here is skill or cleverness, so displaying it is being clever and inventive.

clue.text: Possible venal deeds unknown in among saints?

definitions.text: Possible venal deeds unknown in among saints?

indicators.note: a possible arrangement of letters suggests reworking them

parts.note: taken as written
Y is one of the algebraic unknowns

indicators.note: the first piece is placed among the letters of the next

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for saint, so two saints give SS
taken as written

explanation.surface: A suggestion that corrupt acts are unheard of in the company of saints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possible' rearranges the letters of VENAL DEEDS. Y is the algebraic unknown. The whole clue points to the deadly sins, corrupt deeds no saint would commit.
explanation.definitionFit: The deadly sins are the traditional seven vices such as greed and lust, venal deeds par excellence.

clue.text: Aptitude for living with manliness getting sailor taken for queen

indicators.note: one piece is taken in place of the other

parts.note: virility is manliness
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A man's capacity to live fully on board, swapping royalty for a seaman.
explanation.walkthrough: In VIRILITY the R is replaced by AB.
explanation.definitionFit: Viability is the ability to survive or live successfully.

clue.text: How Dante might have produced a not so great velum

definitions.text: How Dante might have produced a not so great velum

parts.words: How Dante might have produced a not so great velum
parts.note: the velum is the soft palate used in speaking, so a lesser voice from an Italian is speaking quietly, in Italian terms

explanation.walkthrough: The Italian phrase literally means under the voice, the reduced sound the clue's 'not so great velum' produces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sotto voce is an Italian phrase meaning in an undertone or quietly.

clue.text: Small child eats caps with fungus — it's better now

indicators.note: one piece eats, or swallows, the others

parts.note: a tike or tyke is a small child
caps are hats
a morel is an edible fungus
the word it, with the 's as a link

explanation.surface: A youngster munching mushroom caps and saying things are improving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caps' looks like part of the mushroom picture, but here it simply means hats. TIKE is a variant spelling of tyke.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an exclamation of approval meaning things are improving or better now.

clue.text: Herb Lear's daughter used to break Fool's heart

indicators.note: the second piece breaks into the first
heart is the middle letters of the word

parts.note: Regan is one of King Lear's daughters

explanation.surface: King Lear's daughter breaking the heart of the Fool, from the play.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fool is also a character in King Lear, so the surface stays inside the play while 'Fool's heart' only supplies its middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is an aromatic culinary herb.

clue.text: English inclined to keep grand and stylish

indicators.note: the piece keeps, or holds, the next inside

parts.note: leant means inclined
G is slang for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: An Englishman with a taste for luxury and style.
explanation.walkthrough: LEANT keeps G inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means graceful and stylish in appearance.

clue.text: Poor gripe about wicked advantage given only to a few

definitions.text: advantage given only to a few

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, around, the next piece
poor means badly made, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
vile means wicked

explanation.surface: A complaint about an unfairly granted benefit enjoyed by a select few.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges GRIPE to PRIGE, which goes 'about' VILE.
explanation.definitionFit: A privilege is a special right or benefit enjoyed by a limited group.

clue.text: Philosopher with place at centre of Symposium

indicators.note: the centre is the middle letter of the word

explanation.surface: A philosopher takes the central role at a learned gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of the nine-letter SYMPOSIUM is O. Plato wrote a dialogue called the Symposium.
explanation.definitionFit: Plato was the ancient Greek philosopher, pupil of Socrates.

clue.text: California can cut down old tree

parts.note: CA is the postal abbreviation for California

indicators.note: cut down means shortened, so its last letter goes

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Californian being able to fell an ancient tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' trims CAN to CA.
explanation.definitionFit: The cacao is the tropical tree whose seeds give cocoa and chocolate.

clue.text: Want to party wildly, going on from clubs

indicators.note: the second piece carries on after the first

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in cards
to rave is to party wildly

explanation.surface: A desire to dance wildly after leaving the nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' suggests nightclubs, but it is the card suit, C.
explanation.definitionFit: To crave something is to want it intensely.

clue.text: Opening a lair, I braved Arabian brigands' anger

definitions.text: Opening a lair, I braved Arabian brigands' anger

indicators.note: the opening letters of each following word are taken

explanation.surface: A tale-teller boasts of opening a robbers' cave and facing the bandits' fury.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of the seven words after 'Opening' spell the name. The whole clue tells the story, as he opened the thieves' cave and risked their wrath.
explanation.definitionFit: Ali Baba is the woodcutter in the Arabian Nights who opened the forty thieves' cave.

clue.text: Orchestra's lively giving out new volume when Mantovani is playing

indicators.note: giving out means letting go, so the next letters are removed
playing means the letters are moved about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Mantovani's light orchestra sounds bright and lively when it plays.
explanation.walkthrough: MANTOVANI 'giving out' N and V leaves MATOAIN, rearranged as the answer. Mantovani led a popular easy-listening orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Animato is a musical direction telling performers to play in a lively, animated way.

clue.text: Yorick's heading off to speak, the beast

indicators.note: to speak means said out loud, so the letters are the sound

parts.note: the name Yorick's without its first letter Y

explanation.surface: Poor Yorick, beheaded, speaks of an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops the Y of Yorick's, leaving ORICK'S, which sounds like the answer. Yorick is the dead jester whose skull Hamlet holds.
explanation.definitionFit: The oryx is a large African and Arabian antelope with long straight horns.

clue.text: EU national needing guts to work with Europe

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A citizen of an EU country who needs courage to find a job in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to work' rearranges GUTS and EUROPE together.
explanation.definitionFit: A Portuguese person is a citizen of Portugal, a member of the European Union.
